blocks.title: Partnerships
blocks.text:
The Processing Foundation’s core principles of accessibility and empowerment are facilitated through community partnerships.
 
The Foundation works with groups who have historically not had access to the fields of technology, code, and art, whether because of race, gender, class, sexuality, and/or disability.
 
By facilitating dialogue and collaboration, the Foundation sponsors and hosts events that aim to broaden the audience for our software projects, welcome those new to the community, and nurture the specific needs of different groups.

partnerships.title: Emmanuel College
partnerships.description: Processing Foundation partnered with Emmanuel College to support computer science undergraduates to contribute to Processing Java.

partnerships.title: University of Washington
partnerships.description: Processing Foundation partnered with the UW’s Human Centered Design & Engineering department to conduct usability studies of the p5.js website.

partnerships.title: New York University
partnerships.subtitle: Tandon School of Engineering
partnerships.description: Processing Foundation partnered with NYU Integrated Design and Media program, supporting graduate students to research and develop a beginner-friendly introduction to the Rust programming language.

partnerships.title: University of California, Santa Cruz
partnerships.description: Processing Foundation partnered with UCSC’s Open Source Program Office to support undergraduate students from Historically Black Colleges and Universities to contribute to p5.js.

partnerships.title: CodeDay
partnerships.description: Processing Foundation served as an industry mentor for CodeDay, supporting young people worldwide as they contributed to p5.js.

partnerships.title: New York University
partnerships.subtitle: Tandon School of Engineering
partnerships.description: Learning to Teach, Teaching to Learn is an annual conference for educators teaching in creative fields like computational art and design, creative technology, emerging media, and digital humanities.

partnerships.title: The University of Texas at Austin
partnerships.subtitle: WeTeach_CS, Texas Advanced Computing Center
partnerships.description: WeTeach_CS (WTCS) is a teacher professional development program that empowers K-12 educators to integrate computer science education in their classrooms. WeTeach_CS’s support has provided creative coding workshops to art educators across Texas.

partnerships.title: Kadenze
partnerships.description: Processing Foundation partnered with Kadenze, an online educational platform, to create [“Nature of Code”](https://www.kadenze.com/courses/the-nature-of-code-ii/info) and [“Introduction to Programming for the Visual Arts with p5.js.”](https://www.kadenze.com/courses/introduction-to-programming-for-the-visual-arts-with-p5-js/info)
